catalog_quote: Kipsigis has three phonemic tones: High (H), Low (L), and a contour high-falling tone (HL). While H and L can appear on any syllable, the contour tone is only attested on long vowels and, somewhat more rarely, on syllables with a short vowel and a sonorant coda. ... Kipsigis, like other Kalenjin dialects, exhibits a small number of tonal processes, which are all limited to interactions between adjacent tones or tones associated to adjacent morae or syllables. In other words, tone in Kipsigis is not very mobile and we never find long-distance tonal phenomena, or tones that appear far from their underlying position. Furthermore, the language has the typologically rare property of completely lacking downstep (Creider 1982). [Kouneli 2019:30-31] || Vowels only have tones in Kipsigiis. There are four main tones in Kipsigiis. [Toweett 1975:xviii]
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: The Kouneli 2019 passage is in lines 2075-2105 (sec. 3.3 'Tone', printed pp.30-31) word for word; the '..' skips four sentences on contour-tone restriction and TBU = mora. I read the whole phonology sketch (sec. 3, pp.18-35): H, L, HL; mora TBU; no downstep; local sandhi; tonal nominative; 'stress'/'accent' occur nowhere (only hits are a Kipsigis-language acknowledgement word 'kiastressed' and a Spanish-stress reference). Toweett 1975 'Notes on phonology' sec. XVIII (p.xviii) likewise gives four tones and nothing on stress. Identity fine: Kouneli's consultants are Kipsigis speakers (Kericho area); Toweett writes on 'Kipsigiis'; not Nandi or another Kalenjin lect. So the reader's repo…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kipsigis is described purely as a lexical/grammatical tone language (H, L, HL; mora as TBU; tonal nominative case; local sandhi). The most detailed open phonological sketch (Kouneli 2019, 17 pp.) and Toweett's 1975 Kipsigis phonology notes ('Vowels only have tones in Kipsigiis. There are four main tones..', p.xviii) say nothing about word stress or accent placement; no open source states where stress falls or that there is none.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing said in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. (Tonal: contour HL barred on monomoraic syllables; *HL.HL repaired by mora deletion; word-final H -> L before a word-initial H.)
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical tone from elicited citation/NP forms; one sandhi rule operates across word boundaries. An explicit Kalenjin-wide 'Druckakzent' (stress accent) subsection exists in Rottland 1982 sec.5.1.3.2 (p.77-78) but could not be opened, so whether Kipsigis has a (predictable) stress accent alongside tone remains unverified here.
new_statements.identity_note: All opened sources describe Kipsigis proper (kips1239; Toweett 1975 calls it 'Kaaleenychiin (Kipsigiis)', Rottland 'Kipsikiis', older literature 'Lumbwa'); Kouneli's consultants came from three Kipsigis-speaking areas of western Kenya (Kericho region). Rottland 1982 and Tucker 1964/1966 treat 'Kalenjin' (macro-language kale1246) as a whole, Nandi-Kipsigis based; Nandi (nand1266) is already in the catalog as tonal, so a Kipsigis entry is a separate language-level node, not a duplicate.

sources.note: Nothing on stress/accent anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent + read of the whole phonology sketch). Describes Kipsigis as having three phonemic tones (H, L, HL contour restricted to bimoraic syllables), TBU = mora, no downstep, only local tonal processes (H lowering, rising simplification, vowel shortening under *HL.HL, H->L sandhi before H across a word boundary), tonal nominative case.
